isv-success-program.title: ISV Success – Microsoft Partner Center
isv-success-program.notes: ISV Success is a twelve-month program inside the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program for software development companies. It is meant for firms that build business-to-business applications on or integrated with the Microsoft cloud and want to publish them in Microsoft Marketplace. To join, the company must not be headquartered in an embargoed country and needs an application project that is externally available, intended for recurring sales and has at least one assigned developer. Participants commit to start development within a few months, finish within the year and publish to the marketplace. The core package bundles Azure sponsorship credit, an Azure support plan, a Microsoft 365 developer subscription, Dynamics 365 sandboxes, Visual Studio Enterprise, GitHub Enterprise Cloud for new customers and one-to-one guidance on design, go-to-market and listing optimization. Benefits are activated in Partner Center under Benefits. Larger packages exist for existing participants and for companies with a certified software designation, but they depend on Microsoft's discretion. The program can be renewed for a further year once an offer has been published or made transactable and a renewal fee is paid. Sales and marketing benefits require a marketplace listing.

mail-flow-rule.title: Manage mail flow rules in Exchange Online – Microsoft Learn
mail-flow-rule.notes: Mail flow rules, also called transport rules, let an Exchange Online organization inspect messages passing through it and act on them when certain conditions match. A rule consists of conditions, actions and optional exceptions. Typical actions include prepending text to the subject, forwarding a message for approval, sending a policy tip to the sender or generating an incident report. Further settings cover the rule mode (enforce, or test with or without policy tips), a severity value that only filters reports, a time window for activation, a setting to stop processing further rules and a choice of whether to match the sender address in the header, the envelope or both. Rules are processed in priority order, with the top rule evaluated first. Admins can manage them in the Exchange admin center or with Exchange Online PowerShell, and rules created in the admin center start out disabled. The page shows an example that tags external mail sent to a distribution group. Changes can take a while to apply, report data can lag, and the page advises testing each rule and the combination of rules thoroughly.

microsoft-365-message-center.title: Manage Message center – Microsoft 365 admin
microsoft-365-message-center.notes: The Message center is a view in the Microsoft 365 admin center, found under Health, that informs IT admins about upcoming changes, feature updates and required actions across services. It is also reachable through the Microsoft 365 Admin mobile app with push notifications. Posts fall into three categories: prevent or fix issues, plan for change and stay informed. A relevance recommendation of high, medium or low is based on service usage and expected impact, and major updates are announced well ahead when action is required. For some features an organization-specific rollout status such as scheduled, rolling out or launched is shown. Admins can filter by service, tag, category and timing, pick which services appear, configure a weekly digest email and share posts or copy links. Archiving applies only to the individual admin account. Posts can be synced to Planner or read through the Microsoft Graph service communications API. Most admin roles can see the Message center, and a dedicated Message center reader role grants read and share access without other admin rights. Release status and usage figures are only available for part of the content.

microsoft-pluton.title: Microsoft Pluton security processor – Microsoft Learn
microsoft-pluton.notes: Microsoft Pluton is a cryptographic security processor integrated into the CPU or system-on-chip, made up of a secure hardware subsystem and Microsoft-owned software running on it. Microsoft designed it and silicon partners build it. Its purpose is to provide a hardware root of trust, secure identity, secure attestation and cryptographic services, protecting credentials, identities, personal data and encryption keys. It is meant to cover the functions of a Trusted Platform Module and to add capabilities beyond the TPM 2.0 specification. The hardware includes a secure element with a trusted execution environment. Firmware authorized by Microsoft is stored in the motherboard's SPI flash and loaded at boot, and Windows uses the newest available version. Updates arrive through Windows Update or classic UEFI capsule updates. Pluton is documented for Windows 11 on supported editions such as Pro, Enterprise and Education, with listed AMD, Intel and Qualcomm processors. A typical use is acting as the system TPM and supporting device-based conditional access in Intune, where device health is confirmed through tamper-resistant, cryptographically verifiable logs. That conditional access benefit applies only when Pluton is configured as the TPM.

microsoft-purview-records-management.title: Learn about records management – Microsoft Purview
microsoft-purview-records-management.notes: Records management in Microsoft Purview helps organizations handle content that has regulatory, legal or business-critical importance. It supports meeting legal obligations, demonstrating compliance and disposing of content that no longer needs to be kept. Retention labels can mark items as a record or a regulatory record, applied manually or automatically based on sensitive information, keywords or content types. Organizations can import or build a file plan, define retention periods based on creation or modification date, and use event-based retention that starts when a trigger occurs. Disposition reviews, proof of deletion and export of deleted items support the end of the lifecycle. Specific roles control access to records manager functions. A locked record blocks editing and deletion in SharePoint and OneDrive, while a regulatory record is stricter: the label cannot be removed or changed, not even by a global administrator, and retention can only be extended. Regulatory records must be enabled with PowerShell first and cannot come from auto-labeling policies. Exchange only follows locked-record behavior. The page also describes verifying migrated files by comparing hash values. Licensing is covered elsewhere in the documentation.

operator-connect.title: Plan for Operator Connect – Microsoft Teams
operator-connect.notes: Operator Connect links Microsoft Teams Phone to the public switched telephone network through a Microsoft-certified operator. The operator runs the PSTN infrastructure, while administrators manage users in the Teams admin center. The aim is simpler Teams Phone deployment without running and maintaining your own session border controllers, and it lets an organization keep working with an existing operator that participates in the program. Admins enable the chosen operator in the Teams admin center, assign phone numbers, buy new numbers, port existing ones or migrate users from another Teams Phone PSTN option. Prerequisites include the required Teams Phone licenses, users in Teams Only mode, suitable admin permissions, a certified operator available in the target countries or regions and a network that meets Teams requirements. Onboarding runs through four steps: check prerequisites, choose an operator, plan a number strategy and configure Operator Connect. Responsibilities are split. Microsoft covers Teams services and administration, while the operator handles PSTN connectivity, number provisioning and porting, calling services and PSTN-related support. Operator Connect is only one of several PSTN connectivity options.

policy-tip.title: Data loss prevention policy tips reference – Microsoft Purview
policy-tip.notes: A policy tip is a notice shown by a data loss prevention policy to tell users that the content they work with conflicts with a DLP rule. The reference describes where such tips appear and how they differ by application. In Outlook there are default and customized oversharing dialogs, a wait-on-send dialog and a custom compliance link for further user education, with availability depending on the client. In Teams, a flagged message shows a prompt where users can review the detected sensitive information types and, if the admin allows it, override or report a mistake. Supported conditions include content shared from Microsoft 365, sensitive information types, sensitivity labels, subject or body keywords and sender or recipient conditions. Support varies widely: policy tips work in SharePoint and OneDrive on the web, Office apps on the web for documents already stamped by a policy, Teams messages, endpoint devices and Fabric and Power BI. They are not available in SharePoint and OneDrive desktop clients, mobile Office apps, third-party cloud apps or on-premises content. Teams files get no tips, and Windows Office apps show them only for a limited set of conditions and actions.

provisioned-throughput-units.title: Provisioned throughput – Microsoft Foundry
provisioned-throughput-units.notes: A provisioned throughput unit is the unit of measure for provisioned deployments in Microsoft Foundry, where each unit represents a fixed amount of model processing capacity. The chosen number of units is reserved exclusively for the deployment whether or not requests arrive, giving predictable latency compared with standard deployments that share capacity. The page positions it for steady traffic, latency-sensitive applications, high production volumes and real-time scenarios such as chats, copilots or agents. Quota is model-independent but granted per subscription, region and deployment type, and each model has a minimum unit count and its own tokens-per-minute yield per unit. Billing is hourly per unit regardless of tokens consumed, with Azure Reservations as a discounted commitment option. Deployment types include global, data zone and regional provisioned. An optional spillover feature sends overflow requests to a standard deployment, but it is not available for every model family. Sizing relies on request rates, prompt and response sizes and cache rates, supported by a capacity calculator in the portal. Quota does not guarantee capacity, which can fluctuate, and reservations do not guarantee it either, so creating the deployment first is advised.

responsible-ai-dashboard.title: Assess AI systems with the Responsible AI dashboard – Azure Machine Learning
responsible-ai-dashboard.notes: The Responsible AI dashboard is a single interface in Azure Machine Learning that brings several responsible AI tools together for evaluating and debugging models and supporting data-driven decisions. It can be customized so that only the tools relevant to a use case are included, and it is accompanied by a PDF scorecard that exports responsible AI metadata and findings. Its components are data analysis, a model overview with fairness assessment based on Fairlearn, error analysis to locate cohorts where a model fails, model interpretability for global and local feature importance, counterfactual what-if analysis and causal analysis of treatment features. These can be created through the Azure Machine Learning CLI v2, the Python SDK v2 or the studio. Typical flows combine components, for example moving from model overview to error analysis to data analysis, or from data analysis to causal inference to separate correlation from causation. Intended audiences include data scientists and risk officers. Limits: it supports regression and classification on tabular data, only registered MLflow scikit-learn style models, parquet pandas datasets, a capped number of visualized points, and no AutoML models. Mitigation is handled by separate tools.

revoscaler.title: RevoScaleR package – SQL Server Machine Learning Services
revoscaler.notes: RevoScaleR is a Microsoft R package that supports distributed computing, remote compute contexts and high-performance data science algorithms. It covers data import, transformation, summary, visualization and analysis, and it ships with SQL Server Machine Learning Services and SQL Server 2016 R Services. Unlike base R, its functions work on large data sets in parallel and on distributed file systems, processing data that does not fit in memory in chunks and merging the results afterwards. Functions carry an rx or Rx prefix. The reference groups them into data sources and compute contexts, DDL helpers, ETL functions such as rxImport and rxDataStep, plotting functions, descriptive statistics and modeling functions such as linear models, logistic regression, decision trees, forests and k-means. A typical workflow is to develop locally with a SQL Server compute context, for instance to train a model on the server and avoid moving data, and then wrap the finished R code in sp_execute_external_script, ideally as one function with defined inputs and outputs. Limits include no support for stored procedure calls as a data source, some statistics functions that do not chunk data and output restrictions on rxPredict and rxSummary.

self-service-password-reset.title: How Microsoft Entra self-service password reset works – Microsoft Learn
self-service-password-reset.notes: Microsoft Entra self-service password reset lets users change or reset their password, and unlock a blocked account, without involving an administrator or the help desk. The goal is to reduce support calls and lost productivity when people cannot sign in. Users reach a reset portal and register their authentication data through a separate registration page, and registration can optionally be enforced at sign-in. Admins decide whether one or two methods are required and can ask users to reconfirm their details periodically. Available methods include the Microsoft Authenticator app, software and hardware OATH tokens, SMS, voice call and email one-time passcodes. Users receive an email after a reset, and global administrators are notified when other administrators use the feature. Where passwords are managed on-premises, for example with password hash sync or pass-through authentication, password writeback through Microsoft Entra Connect or Cloud Sync is required. Limits: users without enough registered methods must ask an admin, changing the required methods can lock people out, administrator accounts follow a stricter policy, and personal Microsoft accounts invited as guests cannot use it. The page does not list license requirements.

sharepoint-home-site.title: Get started with SharePoint home site – Microsoft Learn
sharepoint-home-site.notes: A SharePoint home site is a communication site with special capabilities that serves as the branded landing point of an organization's intranet and as an entry to other portals. It also forms the base for the SharePoint app in Teams, formerly Viva Connections. The page frames it as an addition to the intranet design rather than a replacement, and recommends using the organization's root site. Key capabilities are intranet-wide search across sites, news and files, a role as the default official source of organization news that gets priority on the SharePoint start page, and global navigation in the SharePoint app bar, which can only be edited from the home site's own start page. Building involves creating the communication site, enabling audience targeting, setting up page approval, swapping the root site before designating the home site and checking performance with page diagnostics. Licensing for a Connections experience requires enterprise, frontline or academic licenses, with more experiences needing Viva licensing. Limits: integration with the SharePoint start page is not available, so a featured link is suggested, and designating the home site before the root swap can lose settings.

sharepoint-hub-sites.title: Planning your SharePoint hub sites – Microsoft Learn
sharepoint-hub-sites.notes: SharePoint hub sites organize an intranet by connecting families of team sites and communication sites. They express relationships as associations rather than hierarchy or ownership, so sites can move between hubs without changing URLs. A hub is usually created from a communication site. Associated sites inherit the hub's theme and shared navigation, and hub web parts such as News, Highlighted content, Sites and Events can roll up content from all associated sites or a chosen subset. The hub also provides a search scope covering its sites, and hubs can be associated with each other to widen that scope. Creating a hub needs SharePoint administrator rights, while hub site owners manage it, and admins can control who may associate sites. Association does not change permissions, and rolled-up content is security-trimmed so people only see what they can already access. Typical designs are functional hubs such as HR, finance or IT and regional or location hubs. A site belongs to only one hub, and news flows from associated sites to the hub, not the other way. The page lists recommended and technical limits for hubs, navigation links and search scope. Subsites remain a classic feature. No specific license requirements are stated.

source-of-authority.title: Group source of authority guidance – Microsoft Entra ID
source-of-authority.notes: This page covers the group source of authority in Microsoft Entra ID, which allows management of groups to move from Active Directory Domain Services to the cloud. The aims are more flexibility, modern governance and simpler administration. Converting the source of authority of a group means security groups are afterward managed in the Microsoft Entra admin center and through Microsoft Graph. Cloud-managed groups can be provisioned back to AD DS using Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync, which requires steps such as setting the group scope to universal and mapping the distinguished name through a directory extension. Rollback is only possible when the object's original authority was AD. Typical uses include cleaning up unneeded AD groups, moving distribution lists and mail-enabled security groups to Microsoft 365 groups, and writing Microsoft 365 groups back to AD for on-premises apps. The change applies only to the named group and is not recursive, so nested groups stay on-premises unless converted individually. Local edits to cloud-managed groups in AD are overwritten at the next provisioning, dynamic membership rules are not carried over, and a custom LDAP connector is not supported. Security-enabled Microsoft 365 groups cannot grant Exchange shared mailbox permissions.

sql-database-in-fabric.title: SQL database in Microsoft Fabric overview – Microsoft Learn
sql-database-in-fabric.notes: SQL database in Microsoft Fabric is a developer-friendly transactional database built on the same SQL Database Engine as Azure SQL Database and part of the Fabric Database workload. It serves as an operational OLTP store whose data is automatically replicated into OneLake as Delta Lake parquet files, so it becomes available for analytics almost in real time. An SQL analytics endpoint is created automatically in the workspace. Users can work through a web query editor in the Fabric portal, SSMS, the MSSQL extension for VS Code or GitHub Copilot. Further features include automatic tuning with automatic index creation, vector data types for semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation, row-level and object-level security, customer-managed keys at workspace level, SQL auditing, sharing without workspace access, Git integration and a GraphQL API. Access is authenticated with Microsoft Entra and needs read permission on the database item, and billing runs through Fabric capacity. Typical scenarios are intelligent applications, reverse ETL, operational data stores and translytical applications. Limits: only the default connection policy is supported, elastic pools in the Azure SQL sense do not exist, and some monitoring features are in preview.

store-commerce-app.title: Store Commerce app – Dynamics 365 Commerce
store-commerce-app.notes: The Store Commerce app is a Windows point-of-sale application for Dynamics 365 Commerce. It is built on a WPF shell that hosts the Microsoft Edge WebView2 control to display Store Commerce for web, so it combines Modern POS and Cloud POS in one application and renders its interface with the Chromium engine instead of the UWP framework. It serves cashiers, sales associates, inventory and warehouse staff and store managers. Functions include cash-and-carry sales, register and shift management, customer engagement, assisted selling, endless aisle, order fulfillment, inventory handling, reporting. Two deployment variants exist: in-app, where all components run locally and offline mode is supported, and hybrid, where the interface loads from the Commerce Scale Unit and offline mode is not available. Requirements include a supported Windows 10, Windows 11 or Windows Server edition, WebView2, the listed .NET runtimes, SQL Server for offline use and a Commerce headquarters environment where the register and device are configured. Limits: ARM processors are unsupported, the app must not run with elevated rights, UWP point-of-service devices are not supported and need OPOS drivers instead. MPOS and hybrid apps were deprecated.

subscription-vending.title: Subscription vending – Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure
subscription-vending.notes: Subscription vending is a platform mechanism for issuing Azure subscriptions programmatically to workload teams that need to deploy workloads. It builds on subscription democratization and treats subscriptions, rather than resource groups, as the main unit of management and scale for workload landing zones. The goal is to standardize and automate how subscriptions are requested, provisioned and governed, giving teams an official front door while keeping governance effort low for platform teams. Roles are split: the cloud center of excellence defines business logic and approval, workload teams request subscriptions, adjust budgets and run the workload, and the platform team creates and configures the subscription before handing it over. The process covers approval, networking without overlapping IP ranges, management group placement and quota checks, creation through infrastructure as code with Bicep or Terraform modules, consistent tags, identity and RBAC and an initial budget. Programmatic creation requires an Enterprise Agreement, Microsoft Customer Agreement or Microsoft Partner Agreement, while configuration can be automated without one. Limits: budgets are monitoring tools and not hard limits, quota requests can fail and workload identities cannot use PIM.

windows-365-link.title: Windows 365 Link overview – Microsoft Learn
windows-365-link.notes: Windows 365 Link is a purpose-built Microsoft device that lets users connect directly to their Cloud PC virtual machine. After signing in on the device, the connection to the Cloud PC is established through the Windows 365 service. Organizations manage these devices with Microsoft Intune together with their other devices. Security features listed on the page include a discrete TPM, Secure Boot, virtualization-based security, hypervisor-protected code integrity, BitLocker encryption, a strict application control policy, security baseline policies enabled by default and the Microsoft Defender endpoint detection sensor. The device supports redirection of web multimedia content to run locally. Requirements are the device itself, management through Intune and a Windows 365 license for the Cloud PC. Because the device is only a client for the cloud session, it has no local user with administrator rights, no local data storage and no local apps. The overview does not cover ports, software details, pricing, supported regions or network requirements, and refers to other pages such as what's in the box for hardware contents.

windows-subsystem-for-linux.title: Windows Subsystem for Linux documentation – Microsoft Learn
windows-subsystem-for-linux.notes: Windows Subsystem for Linux lets developers run a GNU/Linux environment, including most command-line tools, utilities and applications, directly on Windows. Linux runs unmodified and without the overhead of a traditional virtual machine or a dual-boot setup. The documentation highlights uses such as Node.js and web development, scripting and remote development with Visual Studio Code, and its linked videos cover GPU-accelerated machine learning with WSL 2 and running Linux GUI apps. Two versions exist, WSL 1 and WSL 2, compared on a dedicated page. Distributions can be obtained from the Microsoft Store, and other distributions can be used as well. Further topics include accessing Linux files from Windows and Windows files from WSL, connecting USB devices to WSL 2 and a memory reclaim feature. A blog post announces that WSL is open source. Installation guides exist for Windows, for Windows Server and for manual setups. Preview builds are available through the Windows Insiders channels Dev, Beta and Release Preview, which differ in stability. Issues are tracked on GitHub. This landing page does not state system requirements, licensing terms or concrete limitations, and points to the install, comparison and FAQ pages for them.

winui.title: WinUI – Windows apps – Microsoft Learn
winui.notes: WinUI 3 is described as the recommended native UI framework for new Windows desktop applications. It supports C# and C++ with a XAML-based programming model and is part of the Windows App SDK. The framework is meant for modern, responsive desktop apps that follow the Fluent Design System and use high-performance rendering. It offers a broad set of modern controls and styles, advanced pixel processing, high-DPI rendering, smooth animations and input from touch, pen, keyboard and mouse. Apps can run on x86, x64 and ARM devices and reach modern Windows APIs together with tooling for development and deployment through the Windows App SDK. WinUI runs on Windows 10 version 1809 and later, including Windows 11. Parts of the Windows shell and built-in apps are built with WinUI, and PowerToys is cited as an open-source example. The project is developed in public on GitHub in the microsoft-ui-xaml repository and accepts contributions. Getting started material includes a project walkthrough, the WinUI 3 Gallery with interactive control samples, and tools and samples. The page targets Windows desktop apps and states no licensing terms or explicit technical limitations.

az-140.title: Microsoft Certified: Azure Virtual Desktop Specialty – Microsoft Learn
az-140.notes: The Azure Virtual Desktop Specialty certification is earned by passing exam AZ-140. It is an intermediate-level credential for administrators and covers planning, delivering, managing and monitoring virtual desktop experiences and remote apps on Azure for any device. It is aimed at server or desktop administrators who design, implement, manage and maintain Azure Virtual Desktop. The exam is organized into four areas: planning and implementing the infrastructure, planning and implementing identity and security, planning and implementing user environments and apps, and monitoring and maintaining the infrastructure. Candidates are expected to have experience with Azure compute, networking, identity, storage and resiliency, and to use the Azure portal and scripting tools. The exam is proctored, may include interactive components, is offered in several languages and is booked through Pearson VUE, with a personal Microsoft account recommended over a work or school account. Pricing depends on country or region, and retakes are possible after a waiting period. The certification must be renewed, and renewal is free through an online assessment on Microsoft Learn. The page names no formal prerequisites or licensing needs.

sc-401.title: Microsoft Certified: Information Security Administrator Associate – Microsoft Learn
sc-401.notes: The Information Security Administrator Associate certification is based on exam SC-401 and sits at the intermediate level for administrators working in information protection and governance. According to the page, these professionals plan and implement information security for sensitive data using Microsoft Purview and related services. Their goals are protecting data in Microsoft 365 collaboration environments from internal and external threats, protecting data used by AI services and helping respond to information security incidents. Responsibilities include implementing information protection, data loss prevention and retention, handling insider risk management and managing alerts and activities. They work together with governance, data and security roles. Recommended knowledge covers Microsoft 365 services, PowerShell and Microsoft Entra. The exam is proctored, may contain interactive elements, is offered in several languages and is scheduled through Pearson VUE. Price varies by country or region, and a retake is allowed after a waiting period. Role-based certifications expire unless renewed, and renewal is free via an online assessment. The page lists no formal prerequisites and no license requirements.

md-102.title: Microsoft 365 Certified: Endpoint Administrator Associate – Microsoft Learn
md-102.notes: This certification page describes the profile of the Endpoint Administrator, a role that deploys, configures, protects, manages and monitors devices and client applications in a Microsoft 365 environment. Candidates manage identity, security, access, policies, updates and apps for endpoints and handle devices across different operating systems, platforms and device types. At scale this work relies on Microsoft Intune, Windows 365, Windows Autopilot, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Microsoft Entra ID. Endpoint administrators collaborate with architects, Microsoft 365 administrators, security administrators and workload administrators to plan and carry out a modern workplace strategy. Expected experience includes Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365 technologies such as Intune, along with deploying, configuring and maintaining Windows clients and non-Windows devices. The page states a passing score and notes that the English exam version was updated with localized versions following later, with a study guide describing the changes. It does not mention license requirements, costs, exam length, question count or prerequisite certifications, and it describes typical use only indirectly through the role description.

dp-700.title: Microsoft Certified: Fabric Data Engineer Associate – Microsoft Learn
dp-700.notes: The Fabric Data Engineer Associate certification is earned through exam DP-700 and targets data engineers working with Microsoft Fabric at an intermediate level. It is meant to demonstrate expertise in data loading patterns, data architectures and orchestration processes. The role covers ingesting and transforming data, securing and managing an analytics solution, and monitoring and optimizing an analytics solution. Data engineers work closely with analytics engineers, architects, analysts and administrators to design and deploy data engineering solutions for analytics, and need skills in SQL, PySpark and Kusto Query Language. The exam covers three areas: implementing and managing an analytics solution, ingesting and transforming data, and monitoring and optimizing an analytics solution. It is proctored, may include interactive components, is available in many languages and is booked through Pearson VUE. Pricing depends on country or region, and a retake is possible after a waiting period. Certifications expire unless renewed, and renewal is free through an online assessment. The page names no formal prerequisites and says nothing about Fabric licensing.

ab-100.title: Microsoft Certified: Agentic AI Business Solutions Architect Expert – Microsoft Learn
ab-100.notes: The Agentic AI Business Solutions Architect Expert certification is built around exam AB-100 and describes a solution architect who drives the transformation of business processes through AI-powered architectures. It validates the ability to design and implement AI and agent-based business solutions that span several Microsoft services. Listed skills include generative AI and Azure AI services, Azure OpenAI, agent-oriented design, multi-agent orchestration, Copilot Studio, Azure AI Foundry, Dynamics 365 and Power Platform, as well as open standards such as Agent2Agent and the Model Context Protocol. Further themes are responsible AI, securing models and data flows and monitoring and telemetry. Responsibilities include architecture strategy, a roadmap for agent-oriented processes, guidance during implementation and an application lifecycle and environment strategy. To earn the credential, candidates pass AB-100 and also hold at least one of a listed set of associate certifications. The exam areas are planning, designing and deploying AI-powered business solutions, each with a stated weighting range. The exam is booked through Pearson VUE. Exam format and validity period are not stated.
